_comment: This file holds what JJ Flexible says and shows, for the audio area. Audio and DSP - devices, levels, transmit audio, filters, noise reduction. EDITING: change the text on the right of the colon; never change the key on the left, and never change anything inside curly braces such as {radio} - those are filled in at run time with the actual radio name, frequency and so on. A key whose text is missing is spoken as the key itself, so if you hear something like connect.radio_found read out literally, that key needs text. YOUR OWN COPY: put a file of this same name in the lexicon folder beside your settings and it layers on top of this one, key by key - you only need the keys you want to change, and everything else keeps working. If your file has a typo in it, it is ignored and this one is used, so a mistake can never stop the program. LADDERS: a key may hold three tiers instead of one string - critical, terse and chatty - which is how one message gets shorter as you turn verbosity down. See docs/planning/active/string-store-contract.md.
_1_shared: Said in several audio places, word for word the same in each. Changing one of these changes every place that says it.

audio.check.loopback_no_free_slice: no free slice for the listening receiver

audio.check.loopback_ended: Loopback ended. Antenna, power, monitor and duplex settings restored.

audio.check.loopback_honesty: You will hear your own signal through an overloaded receiver: it proves your audio is present and processed, not exactly how you sound on the air.
audio.check.loopback_drive_reduced: Transverter drive reduced for a cleaner listen.
audio.check.loopback_proves_chain: This also proves your transmitter chain end to end.

audio.preset.reset_to_defaults: Transmit audio settings reset to defaults
audio.preset.export_failed: The file could not be written to {file}. Nothing was exported.

audio.preset.imported: Imported {preset}. Added to your saved presets; the radio is unchanged until you load it.
audio.preset.save_failed_reason: It could not be saved — there is no operator loaded, so there is no place to keep it yet.
audio.preset.deleted_but_not_saved: Preset {preset} removed from the list, but {reason} It will be back next time.
audio.preset.imported_but_not_saved: {preset} was read from the file, but {reason}
audio.preset.delete_body: This deletes {preset} from your saved presets. There is no undo — to get it back you would save or import it again. Nothing on the radio changes.

audio.noise.folder_open_failed: Could not open the profiles folder
audio.noise.turn_a_stage_on_first: Turn on a PC noise reduction stage first

audio.noise.select_a_profile_first: Select a profile in the list first

audio.noise.nothing_to_save: No noise profile to save. Capture one first.
audio.noise.capture.pc_audio_off: PC audio is off. Noise capture listens to the radio audio playing through this computer. Turn PC audio on first.

audio.noise.capture.no_audio_arriving: Noise capture stopped. No radio audio is reaching this computer. Is PC audio on?
audio.noise.capture.spectral_is_using_it: PC Spectral NR is using it.

_6_micprofile: Microphone profiles: a named capture-plus-sculpt setup, and the silent-transmit repair.
audio.micprofile.none_selected_save_one: No microphone profile is selected. Save one first.
audio.micprofile.deleted_but_not_saved: Microphone profile {profile} was removed from the list, but {reason} It will be back next time.
audio.micprofile.delete_body: This deletes the microphone profile {profile}, including its settings for every radio it was set up on. Profiles stored on a radio itself are not touched. There is no undo.
audio.micprofile.references_radio_profil: On this radio it references mic profile {profile}.
audio.micprofile.created_on_radio: A mic profile named {profile} was created on the radio and referenced.
audio.micprofile.nothing_created_on_radi: Nothing was created on the radio, so your computer settings were saved on their own.
audio.micprofile.snapshotted: The radio's TX settings were snapshotted into it.
audio.micprofile.create_reason: You asked JJ Flex to create a mic profile named {profile} on the radio itself.
audio.micprofile.load_reason: You asked JJ Flex to load the mic profile {profile} on {radio}, so that transmit audio from this computer has somewhere to go.
audio.micprofile.radio_offers_none: This radio does not offer a mic profile to load.
audio.micprofile.loaded_on_radio: Mic profile {profile} loaded on the radio. Transmit audio from this computer has a chain to go through now.
audio.micprofile.no_longer_listed: This radio no longer lists a mic profile named {profile}, so nothing was changed.
audio.micprofile.someone_elses_title: Change a Setting on Someone Else's Radio
audio.micprofile.someone_elses_body: Loading the mic profile {profile} would give transmit audio from this computer a chain to travel through, which is what fixes the problem. It creates nothing new — that profile already exists on the radio.
audio.micprofile.someone_elses_shared: A mic profile is shared. Every program connected to this radio uses the one that is loaded, so its owner and anyone else on it get this change too, with nothing on their end to say why.
audio.micprofile.someone_elses_deliberat: An empty selection can be deliberate. If the radio's owner arranged it that way, this undoes their arrangement.
audio.micprofile.device_mismatch: It was made with {device}; this computer is using {current}, so the Windows input level was left alone.
audio.micprofile.device_mismatch_with_cl: It was made with {device}; this computer is using {current}, so the Windows input level and the transmit cleanup settings were left alone.
audio.micprofile.cleanup_needs_a_radio: Its transmit cleanup settings need a connected radio, so they were not applied.
audio.micprofile.level_not_set: The Windows input level could not be set: {reason}
_7_reference: Reference audio: a known recording sent in place of the microphone.
audio.reference.folder_open_failed: The recordings folder could not be opened.

audio.reference.tone_already_armed: The test tone is armed, and only one thing can replace your microphone at a time. Turn the test tone off first.
audio.reference.armed: Reference armed: {recording}. It replaces your microphone from the start of the recording each time you transmit.
audio.reference.finished: Reference finished. Your microphone is back.

audio.tone.armed: Test tone armed: {freq} hertz at {level} dBFS.
audio.tone.armed_replaces_mic: It replaces your microphone while you transmit.

_17_device_roles: What each device is FOR, in the sentences that name it. Three of these describe the same radio output and word it three different ways today; that is recorded here rather than quietly tidied, because which wording survives is the owner's call. See the Track E report.
